key_insight: A multi-agent AI pipeline extracted transfusion reaction features from clinical notes with precision above 98%, but sensitivity varied from 62.4% to 77.4% across models.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support hemovigilance by identifying reaction-related signals in free-text notes, though clinical deployment was not evaluated.
method: Curated 181 features from the NHSN Hemovigilance Module protocol.
Tested three open-weight language models in a multi-stage pipeline extracting features, timing, and clinical details.
Two physicians independently reviewed outputs from 50 notes in a blinded interface.
evidence_signal: Physicians agreed on 1,201 of 1,343 co-rated feature occurrences (89.4%); among concordant assessments, Kimi K3 had the highest sensitivity at 77.4% (95% CI 74.5–80.0%).
watch_item: Evaluation covered only 50 notes, and omissions accounted for over 94% of false negatives, warranting broader validation before operational use.
paper_title: Multi-Agent Generative Artificial Intelligence for Transfusion Reaction Feature Extraction
